text.p: The International Air Services Commission (IASC) confirmed on Tuesday a draft decision to renew Qantas Airways Ltd's capacity on the Japan route.
The IASC said in a draft decision released on December 23 that it intended to renew Qantas' capacity, a move which blocks rival Ansett Australia from taking up capacity on that route.

"Ansett had applied for capacity, but...the Commission could only grant capacity to Ansett if the Commission first concluded that Qantas had failed to service the route effectively," the IASC said in a statement on Tuesday.
"The Commission did not believe it had grounds to conclude that Qantas had not serviced the route effectively."
Qantas' capacity agreement was due to expire on June 30.
Qantas is 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc. Ansett is jointly owned by News Corp Ltd and Air New Zealand.
